newsitem.title: UK: CBI'S BARKER WARNS AGAINST UK RATE RISE TODAY.
newsitem.headline: CBI'S BARKER WARNS AGAINST UK RATE RISE TODAY.

text.p: The Bank of England's interest rate setting Monetary Policy Committee should not raise British interest rates again on Thursday because it risked tipping the economy into recession, Confederation of British Industry chief economist Kate Barker said.
"I don't think that we ought to see interest rates go up again today," Barker said in a BBC Radio interview.

"We have seen since the election a very big monetary tightening...we've seen interest rates up three-quarters of a (percentage) point and we've seen sterling up a further five percent. That's going to slow the economy next year.
"A further rise in interest rates today risks that slowdown turning into a grinding halt," she said.
The result of the MPC meeting will be revealed at 1100 GMT on Reuters

Barker said that most commentators agreed the British economy was likely to grow at a faster than sustainable rate over the next few months but said that the authorities had already taken steps to cool demand.

"The rise in interest rates we've already had is going to bring that too strong growth to an end next year. We don't need to run the risk of overkill by tightening the monetary screws further today," she added.

Barker said that Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown had missed an opportunity to bear down on consumer demand in his July budget and should have imposed larger personal tax rises but nothing more needed to be done on the monetary side to compensate.
"We need at least to have a pause in putting up interest rates and take better stock of what effect the rises we've already had are going to have on the economy," she said.
Barker said she believed the MPC would hold fire and leave British rates unchanged at 6.75 percent at today's meeting.
However there is speculation in financial markets that the MPC will raise rates to 7.0 percent.
